subject: Re: faster replies to new patients
body:
Hi Sam,

Thanks for the email, and sorry for the slow reply, it has been a hectic few weeks. To give you some background: we run two clinics and a small satellite office, and for the past year our biggest headache has been the gap between when a new patient submits the form on our website and when somebody actually calls them back. Sometimes it is 30 minutes, sometimes it is the next afternoon. We know we lose people in that gap, because we have checked a few times and some of them already booked elsewhere by the time we called.

We had a go at fixing it ourselves with an auto responder in our email system, but it sounded robotic and a couple of patients complained. So when I saw your note about replies that sound like a person, I thought, okay, worth a look. I would like to see an actual example, ideally on a real enquiry, and to understand what happens when someone writes back with something unusual. Our practice manager Dana would need to be in the room because she owns the front desk process.

Could you do next Wednesday or Thursday, afternoon our time (Mountain)? If you send two or three options I will check with Dana.

Thanks,
Priya

subject: Re: intro
body:
Hello Sam. I read through your message twice and I still have several questions, which I will put in a list because that is how my brain works.

First, you say you answer leads in under a minute. Is that a human or software? Second, if it is software, what does it do when a patient asks something clinical, like whether a procedure hurts? I would not want anything giving medical advice. Third, what is the contract term? Fourth, how many practices like ours are using it today? Fifth, what does the setup involve on our side? We are not very technical and our website was built by a cousin.

I am not saying no. I am saying I need more before I can say yes. Thank you for your time.

Regards,
Alma Reyes

subject: Re: lead follow up
body:
Sam, first of all thank you for being polite about this, most vendors are not. I want to be honest with you. The idea is good. If I were reading this a year ago I would have said yes immediately. The situation right now is that we are two weeks away from a move into a new building, half of our team is on leave, and I am personally doing the work of three people. I cannot evaluate anything new and I do not want to say yes and then ghost you. So the honest answer is: not now. After the move settles, which I expect to be around the middle of next quarter, I would be glad to hear from you again. Please do get back in touch then.

Best,
Walt

subject: Re: quick question
body: Hi, I think this email has gone astray. I used to be the marketing coordinator at Northfork Dental but I changed jobs in the summer and now work for a bakery chain, which as you can imagine has nothing to do with patient enquiries. The person who took over my role is called Tess Aldana and I believe her address is tess.aldana@northfork.example.test, though I would double check that on their website. Wishing you luck with it, it sounds like a good product. Please take my old address off your records so it does not bounce around.

subject: Re: Re: faster replies to new patients
body:
Good afternoon.

I have received four emails from your company this month and I have not replied to any of them, because I do not know who you are and I never asked to hear from you. I run a small practice and spend my evenings sorting through a full inbox. I realise you are doing your job, so no hard feelings, but I would be grateful if you would take me off whatever list I have been added to and not contact me again. Thank you for understanding.

Kind regards,
Dr. M. Okonkwo

subject: Re: speed to lead
body:
Please see the questions below and note I would like written answers rather than a call at this stage.
1. Which countries do you send messages from and do you comply with local telemarketing rules?
2. Is a recording of the conversation kept and who can access it?
3. What is the process for a patient asking to be deleted?
4. Does your system ever contact people who have previously told us not to?
5. Who are your sub processors?
6. What is your uptime over the last 12 months?

We will decide after reading your answers. Thank you.
